name: adv_multitask_bad
title: Multi-task learning with uncertainty weighting - ten planted defects
origin: the defective twin of adv_advanced_clean/multitask.py, hardening round 2, 2026-09-14
note: Both MLV702 variants fire here on one class - a dict of heads and a list comprehension of nn.Parameter - which is the defect that silently destroys the method: the learned log-variances are never registered, so the optimizer never moves them and every task keeps its initial weight while the loss still looks like uncertainty weighting. Four other defects are recorded under `unsupported` because the composed objective returned by `weighted_loss()` cannot be typed, which MLView declares: an `untagged_dataflow` diagnostic names `loss.backward()` at line 84 and says the MLV2xx family did not judge this training step.

expected.defect: the three task heads live in a plain Python dict
expected.why: none of them is registered on MultiTaskNet, so .parameters() never yields their weights and all three heads stay at their initialisation

expected.defect: the three learned log-variances are a plain list comprehension of nn.Parameter
expected.why: the optimizer never sees them, so the uncertainty weights never move - the method degenerates into a fixed 1:1:1 sum while still costing three extra parameters

expected.defect: the training loader does not shuffle
expected.why: the four-tensor TensorDataset is consumed in construction order every epoch, so the batch gradients stay correlated
the three per-task predictions come back in a different order each run, so nothing can be aligned across tasks or across runs
the trunk carries nn.BatchNorm1d and nn.Dropout(0.3), so the reported test loss is measured with a randomly thinned network AND the BatchNorm running statistics keep moving during evaluation

expected.defect: evaluate() is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: a full autograd graph is built for every evaluation batch and thrown away

expected.defect: the whole module is pickled instead of its state_dict
expected.why: the checkpoint carries the class path, so it stops loading as soon as the module moves

expected.defect: nothing seeds torch, numpy or random
expected.why: the synthetic data, the parameter initialisation and the dropout masks all move between runs, so the per-task weights a reader compares are not comparable

forbidden.why: optimizer.step() is called at line 83, inside the batch loop
there is no torch.no_grad() anywhere in this file
DEVICE is chosen by torch.cuda.is_available() at line 21
MultiTaskNet.__init__ calls super().__init__() on its first line
there is no split call; the train and test sets are built separately from torch.randn
there is no sklearn transformer in this project

unsupported.defect: optimizer.step() at line 83 runs before loss.backward() at line 84, in the same block of the batch loop
unsupported.why: `weighted_loss()` returns an accumulated arithmetic expression, so `loss` carries no LOSS tag and `.backward()` never earns the BACKWARD role. MLView declares the silence: an `untagged_dataflow` diagnostic names loss.backward() at line 84 and lists MLV201/202/203/205 as the rules that did not judge it.

unsupported.defect: running is created at line 72, outside the batch loop, and accumulates the live composed loss
unsupported.why: same cause as the MLV203 row: the composed loss is untyped, and the silence is declared.

unsupported.defect: the classification logits are softmaxed before CrossEntropyLoss, which log-softmaxes them again
unsupported.why: `class_criterion` arrives by tuple-unpacking a `criteria` parameter, so MLV401 cannot resolve the loss constructor at the call site.

unsupported.defect: raw logits are handed to nn.BCELoss, which expects probabilities in [0, 1] and raises or produces nan on a negative input
unsupported.why: same cause: the criterion arrives by tuple-unpacking a parameter, so the missing_sigmoid variant cannot resolve the loss class.

unsupported.defect: the uncertainty weighting is summed over `model.log_vars[index]`, which are unregistered Parameters, so the `+ log_var` regulariser is a constant and the whole weighting scheme is inert
unsupported.why: the consequence of the MLV702 finding at line 42, one step removed; no rule models `a Parameter read but never optimised`.
